title: MAD Magazine: A Tribute
summary: A tribute to MAD Magazine. The hosts trace its origins from EC Comics and Bill Gaines through the 1954 Senate hearings on comic books and the Comics Code Authority, to the founding of MAD as a humor comic spoofing other comics under Harvey Kurtzman, its switch to magazine format, and its long run with artists like Mort Drucker, Al Jaffee, Antonio Prohias, Sergio Aragones, Don Martin and Dave Berg. They cover Alfred E. Neuman and the lawsuit over his image, the 1961 Irving Berlin parody lawsuit that helped establish parody protections, ad-free publishing, the Simpsons' Spiro Agnew joke, MAD TV, the magazine's decline and its 2019 end of original content, and a listener email about women in trucking. Includes a brief tour announcement at the start.

segments.title: Tour dates and opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts announce fall tour dates in Orlando, Nashville and Atlanta, then open with banter about MAD magazine's name and its early imitators.

segments.title: Childhood fandom of MAD
segments.summary: Hosts recall reading MAD as kids, the magazine's cover price and no-advertising model, and the influence of illustrators Mort Drucker and Angelo Torres.

segments.title: MAD's influence on satire and skepticism
segments.summary: Discussion of MAD's role in laying groundwork for modern satire and teaching kids skepticism, with a quote from Art Spiegelman.

segments.title: EC Comics origins
segments.summary: EC Comics founded by Maxwell Gaines, its early titles, and his son Bill Gaines taking over and turning to horror comics.

segments.title: Comics boom and horror content
segments.summary: Comic sales in the 1950s and the prevalence of crime and horror titles, and MAD's early themes.

segments.title: 1954 Senate hearings on comic books
segments.summary: Psychiatrist Frederic Wertham's claims that comics caused juvenile delinquency, the Senate subcommittee hearings, and the exchange between Bill Gaines and Senator Estes Kefauver over a bloody cover.

segments.title: Gaines's testimony and the fallout
segments.summary: Gaines's defense of comics and his weaker performance under questioning, and the publishers' response forming the Comics Magazine Association of America.

segments.title: Comics Code Authority and birth of MAD
segments.summary: The Comics Code Authority's self-censorship rules, Gaines dropping horror titles, and keeping the humor comic Tales Calculated to Drive You Mad, which became MAD.
topics: Tales Calculated to Drive You Mad

segments.title: Harvey Kurtzman and early parodies
segments.summary: Kurtzman's idea to spoof comics, early parodies like Superduperman and Starchy, and DC Comics' response to earlier spoofs.

segments.title: Switch to magazine format and Kurtzman's departure
segments.summary: MAD switches to a glossy magazine format to escape the Code, Kurtzman's perfectionism and departure, and MAD's ad-free approach that let it spoof advertising.

segments.title: Hugh Hefner's Trump and Kurtzman's later work
segments.summary: Kurtzman's 1956 departure leading to Hefner's Trump and Humbug, Little Annie Fanny, and Al Feldstein taking over and bringing in longtime artists.

segments.title: Feldstein and the What, Me Worry mascot
segments.summary: Feldstein's role and the introduction of the Alfred E. Neuman mascot and 'What, me worry?' slogan.

segments.title: Alfred E. Neuman origins and copyright lawsuit
segments.summary: Origins of the Alfred E. Neuman face traced to an 1894 play, the 1965 Harry Spencer lawsuit, MAD's usage rules, and how the image is public domain.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break.

segments.title: Al Jaffee and the fold-in
segments.summary: Al Jaffee's career and record, retirement and death, and the fold-in feature and staff quota system.

segments.title: Dick DeBartolo, Antonio Prohias and Spy vs Spy
segments.summary: DeBartolo's parody writing, Prohias's Cuban exile and Spy vs Spy's Cold War message, and his hiring.

segments.title: Sergio Aragones and marginals
segments.summary: Sergio Aragones joining MAD and the marginal one-panel cartoons, plus speculation about his bloopers illustrations.

segments.title: Dave Berg
segments.summary: Dave Berg's Lighter Side of... comics, a memorable panel, and his conservative persona.

segments.title: Don Martin and long-running staff
segments.summary: Don Martin's style and comic strips, and how long-tenured staff kept MAD's voice consistent, with the Simpsons Spiro Agnew joke.

segments.title: Sing Along with Mad lawsuit and parody protections
segments.summary: The 1961 Irving Berlin lawsuit over a parody record and the court's statement on parody and satire, plus Weird Al Yankovic's connection and MAD's peak circulation.

segments.title: MAD's decline, LA relaunch and Cracked revival
segments.summary: Decline of the magazine, the later LA-based relaunch, corporate mergers, end of original content in 2019, and Jack O'Brien's revival of Cracked.

segments.title: MAD TV and wrap-up
segments.summary: MAD TV's run and cast, and hosts' closing remarks on the magazine.

segments.title: Listener mail: women in trucking
segments.summary: Listener Amanda from Pittsburgh writes about her work at a third-party logistics company and Women in Trucking.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank listeners and close the episode with the production credit.
